gen-gf-bruno-ace-outfit: Ruler-straight and unhurried, Bruno Ace spaces out its letters one beat at a time. Outfit follows with curves that stop well short of closing, so a long block of text moves along smoothly in plain sans.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-plus-jakarta-sans: Drafted-looking and spaced out, Bruno Ace gives every letter its own beat. Plus Jakarta Sans is the counterweight, a precise monoline plain sans whose curve endings stay well apart, and that restraint is what makes the pair work.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-space-grotesk: Bruno Ace draws each letter with a ruler-straight line and lets the characters linger, one per beat. And Space Grotesk keeps its counters open like a cut reed, so a long passage in plain sans moves along without friction.
gen-eater-fs-familjen-grotesk: Menacing and wide-spaced, Eater has short ascenders and a worn, stamped look in its thick and thin strokes. But Familjen Grotesk is the livelier one, its bowls left unfinished on one side and its lowercase standing tall.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-amulya: Amulya reads modern and open. Its curves leave generous gaps, so a longer stretch of plain sans text stays easy on the eye while Pixelify Sans keeps its steady, pressure-free line up top.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-plein: Chunky and pixel-built, Pixelify Sans keeps one steady line and an open c. Plein is the reliable one, a plain sans that opens a clear channel into each round letter and handles the detail work.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-spline-sans: Blocky, bold and bright, Pixelify Sans lays down a steady line with a wide-open c. Spline Sans settles beneath it as a plain sans with generous gaps at the curve ends, giving the loud heading somewhere quiet to rest.
gen-gf-pixelify-sans-fs-synonym: Bold and pixel-sharp, Pixelify Sans holds one steady line with a wide-open c. Synonym runs on a plain stripe of constant ink with generous openings in every curve, so a long passage in plain sans feels dependable.
gen-gf-shantell-sans-fs-amulya: Shantell Sans has a mouth as wide as a tin can's cut lid and a single fixed nib width, with no pinched joints. Amulya, in contrast, is the quieter sans, modern and generous in its curves.
gen-gf-sniglet-fs-plein: Rounded, flat and loud, Sniglet keeps terminals short of curling and a level line with no weight accents. Plein does the opposite job as a reliable sans-serif, leading a clear channel into each round letter.
